data.title: US Navy ship Wally Schirra docks at L&T Kattupalli for routine repairs
data.description:
The US Navy’s logistics ship, USNS Wally Schirra, arrived at L&T’s Kattupalli shipyard near Chennai on Friday for a “small voyage repair”, demonstrating the country’s growing maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) infrastructure and technical capabilities.

“The contract from US Navy’s Military Sealift Command (MSC) for Voyage Repair Availability (VRA) of USNS Wally Schirra which arrived at the dock on Friday morning is for a small voyage repair but successful execution of this order will help them undertake larger refits in India,” said sources privy to developments in L&T.

The VRA covers routine upkeep, minor hull or mechanical repairs, and emergent fixes performed pier side so the ship can quickly return to active service, elaborated sources.

Specialised Support

This marks the fifth occasion on which a US naval vessel has undertaken repairs at L&T’s modernised facility at Kattupalli under the India-US Master Ship Repair Agreement, as per a statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA).

A Lewis and Clark-class dry cargo and ammunition ship, it provides ocean transportation, logistics and specialised maritime support to US military and government agencies worldwide.

India–US cooperation in ship repairs commenced from August 2022, when USNS Charles Drew became the first US Navy vessel to undergo repairs at an Indian shipyard. USNS Matthew Perry followed in March 2023 and USNS Salvor in July 2023.

As a fallout, L&T’s Kattupalli shipyard signed the Master Ship Repair Agreement with the US Navy in April 2023, institutionalising the cooperation and enabling the shipyard to undertake voyage repairs of US Navy vessels, MEA said.

USNS Charles Drew subsequently returned to Kattupalli for repairs in December 2024.

SOP Eased

Wally Schirra is the first US naval vessel to arrive for repairs after the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) was revised in July, facilitating smooth entry and exit of ship crew. The sector, otherwise, was burdened with long standing bureaucratic and visa bottlenecks regarding Shore Leave Passes (SLPs) and crew sign-on and sign-off procedures for civilian mariners and technicians arriving aboard vessels undergoing maintenance at Indian shipyards.

The revised SOP was finalised through coordinated efforts involving the MEA, Ministry of Home Affairs, Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Defence and Department of Defence Production, reflecting a whole-of-government approach towards facilitating ship-repair operations in India.

Other than the L&T, Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL) and Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) too have inked individual MSRAs with the US Navy between 2023 and 2024. Goa Shipyard Limited and Kolkata Port are also in advanced stages of negotiation for MSRAs.

MRO Potential

“With its strategic location along major international shipping routes, expanding shipyard infrastructure, skilled workforce and growing technical capabilities, India is well positioned to emerge as a hub for ship repair and maintenance across the Indo-Pacific and beyond,” observed the MEA.

The UK Royal Navy’s Royal Fleet Auxiliary (RFA) similarly has contracted Indian yards directly for mid-deployment upkeep, with two British auxiliary vessels have already availed MRO facilities for regular maintenance. Japan is also negotiating for a similar reciprocal pact.

data.title: Canada retail sales rise 0.8% in September; likely to be down 1.5% in October
data.description:
Key points:
  • October retail sales likely fall 1.5%, Statistics Canada says
  • Core retail sales edge up 0.1% in September
  • Gasoline station and fuel vendor sales jump 6.9% in September

By Promit Mukherjee

Canadian retail sales rose 0.8% in September on a monthly basis to C$75.31 billion ($52.58 billion), slightly more than expectations as sales picked up at gasoline stations and fuel vendors, Statistics Canada said on Friday.

The September growth rate was lower than the upwardly revised 1.4% growth in August, and the statistics agency said in a preliminary estimate that sales were likely to be down 1.5% in October.

  • Retail sales, which include purchases of cars, furniture, food and gasoline, are considered an early indicator of gross domestic product growth and account for about 40% of consumer spending

  • Core retail sales, which exclude gasoline stations and fuel vendors and motor vehicle and parts dealers, edged up 0.1% in September, representing 66.9% of retail trade

  • In August, retail sales were higher in five out of nine subsectors. In volume terms, retail sales were up 0.1% in the month

  • Sales at gasoline stations and fuel vendors, which contribute almost a tenth of the total retail sales in the country, were the biggest contributor with 6.9% growth in September

  • Sales of motor vehicles and parts, which is by far the biggest contributor to overall sales and accounts for over a quarter of overall sales, were up 0.2%

  • Sales at food and beverage retailers, the second biggest contributor to retail sales, were down 0.4% in the month

  • The categories of building material and furniture retailers were both down 1.3%, data showed

($1 = 1.4322 Canadian dollars)

data.title: The Dow joins the correction watch
data.description:
Key points:
  • US equity index futures red; Nasdaq 100 down ~1.5%
  • STOXX 600 index slides >1.5%
  • Dollar falls; gold down >1%; US crude slips; bitcoin rises
  • US 10-year Treasury yield falls to ~4.99%

THE DOW JOINS THE CORRECTION WATCH

With the Nasdaq Composite , Nasdaq 100 and Russell 2000 already in correction territory, traders are increasingly watching to see whether the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX and Dow Jones Industrial Average follow suit.

The S&P 500 ended Thursday down 8.2% from its October 6 record close, while the Dow finished 9.7% below its August 5 peak, leaving the blue-chip average just a small step away from the 10% correction threshold.

The Dow's recent decline has accelerated since the November 3 midterm elections and is on track for its biggest monthly drop since March. The index has also fallen four straight days and is headed for its worst weekly loss since the tariff-driven selloff in early April 2025.

Technically, this week's weakness is significant because the Dow has broken below a rising channel that had guided the advance from the spring lows. The average ended Thursday at 49,097.06.

While E-mini Dow futures (YMcv1) are modestly lower ahead of Friday's open, volatility has surged. The Cboe Volatility Index has climbed above 31 and reached its highest level since late March, underscoring heightened uncertainty and the potential for sharp swings in the major indexes.

The Dow’s next key support zone lies in the 48,757-48,708 area, where the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement of the March-August advance aligns closely with the April 29 low.

If that area fails, attention could shift toward the 47,343-47,130 region. That zone includes the maximum Fibonacci retracement range of the March-August rally and lies just above an unfilled April gap that requires a fall to 46,744 for a fill. A decline into this area would leave the Dow roughly 13%-14% below its record high.

A complete round trip to the March 30 intraday low near 45,057 would leave the Dow down more than 17% from its record close.

On the upside, resistance sits near 49,900. More importantly, a recovery above the 50,550-51,050 area, which includes the 200-day moving average and several key chart markers, would suggest the Dow has at least stabilized for now.

data.title: Gold, Silver Drop to Lowest Levels in Over a Year — Update
data.description:
By Megan Cheah and Farhan Rafid

Gold and silver prices fell to their lowest levels in over a year on Friday as a broader selloff across commodities and expectations of higher interest rates globally pressured precious metals.

Expectations for tighter monetary policy appear to have overshadowed the typical demand for gold as a safe haven for risk-averse investors. The precious metals weakened despite heavy losses across Asian stock markets.

December gold futures fell 3.4% to $3,561.70 a troy ounce, while spot silver declined around 2.1% to $41.84 an ounce.

The decline in precious metals is part of a broader selloff across commodities, with investors cutting exposure, unwinding crowded positions and taking profits ahead of year-end, according to Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank.

Hansen said in a note Friday that precious metals had suffered the largest losses, with silver falling 14% and gold nearly 8% this week. Rising borrowing costs, a stronger U.S. dollar and concerns about artificial-intelligence investment have added to selling pressure, while losses in other assets have increased demand for cash.

Gold's failure to attract safe-haven demand during the equity-market selloff suggests investors are selling liquid assets to cover losses and reduce risk, Hansen said. However, holdings in gold exchange-traded funds have remained broadly unchanged over the past month despite the decline in prices, indicating longer-term investors have largely maintained their exposure.

The gold-to-silver ratio rose as high as 85.65 Friday, about 25% above its average over nearly three decades. The ratio measures how many ounces of silver are needed to buy an ounce of gold, with a higher reading indicating silver is relatively cheaper.

Julius Baer analyst Carsten Menke said silver's decline below $45 an ounce, alongside a gold-to-silver ratio above 85, could present a buying opportunity. However, the bank is waiting for signs that prices have bottomed before turning more positive, as further declines remain possible. Julius Baer maintains a neutral view on silver and a constructive outlook for gold.

Copper also declined, with December futures falling 2.4% to $5.4965 a pound. The industrial metal is on track to lose around 9% this week, reaching an eight-month low amid concerns about global growth, Chinese demand and the outlook for artificial-intelligence infrastructure investment, according to Saxo Bank.

Julius Baer upgraded its outlook for copper to constructive following the recent correction, saying the metal remains at risk of a structural supply deficit as demand from electric vehicles, clean energy and battery storage increases. Copper prices have fallen more than 15% from their highs this year, but the bank expects electrification-related technologies to account for around 30% of demand by 2035, compared with 25% in 2025. Menke said mining investments are increasing but might come too late to prevent a shortage.

Japan's consumer inflation data for October, released Friday, showed prices were accelerating past the Bank of Japan's target. That reinforced expectations for tighter policy as policymakers grew increasingly worried about the risk of higher prices due to increased energy costs, persistent yen weakness and rising semiconductor prices amid the artificial-intelligence boom.

"A rate hike at the next meeting in December looks highly likely, and the central bank will likely discuss an additional increase in March 2027, when inflation is expected to accelerate into the 3% range," said Takeshi Minami, an economist at Norinchukin Research Institute.

Minutes from the U.S. Federal Reserve's October meeting, released Wednesday, also showed that nearly all policymakers expected higher interest rates would be needed to lower inflation.

The minutes "showed strong alignment from Fed officials on the need for additional rate hikes," said MUFG analysts. Markets recently priced in a 93% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike next month.

Many also expect the European Central Bank to raise rates in December after staying on hold last month, as it is under pressure to address the inflationary backdrop given persistently high energy prices.

A higher interest-rate environment typically diminishes the allure of nonyielding assets such as gold and silver. The hawkish Fed view also likely lifted the dollar, which makes gold and silver--both dollar-denominated commodities--more expensive for investors holding other currencies.

Upcoming U.S. economic data could shape expectations for the size of a December interest-rate move by the Fed, said Critical Metals' Tony Sage in a note. This includes the second estimate for the country's third-quarter gross domestic product growth due next week.

"Firm readings could lift yields further and extend gold's losses, while softer prints may offer some relief," he added.

data.title: Aprea Therapeutics Reports Interim APR-1051 Phase 1 Results and Plans Focused Expansion
data.description:
Aprea Therapeutics reported interim APR-1051 Phase 1 results showing early responses, WEE1 target engagement and pharmacokinetics supporting once-daily dosing.

Key Highlights:

  • Among 43 evaluable patients, two with PPP2R1A-mutated uterine cancers had partial responses; one was confirmed and ongoing beyond 10 months.
  • Five patients had stable disease lasting at least four months, while 16 patients had stable disease as their best response.
  • WEE1 target engagement was observed in 21 of 25 evaluable patients across multiple dose levels, based on reductions in a pharmacodynamic marker.
  • One dose-limiting toxicity occurred among 56 treated patients; Grade 3 pneumonitis occurred in two patients, and no febrile neutropenia was reported.
  • Aprea plans to enroll at least 50 patients in focused uterine serous carcinoma and cyclin E-overexpressing platinum-resistant ovarian cancer cohorts; dose escalation and backfill enrollment are expected to finish in Q2 2027.

data.title: Saudi Arabia once banned Grand Theft Auto. Now it's got a stake in it
data.description:
Key points:
  • Saudi investments in gaming part of push to move beyond oil
  • Sovereign wealth fund PIF a major backer of firm behind GTA
  • Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman an avid gamer
  • Authorities eased gaming restrictions on GTA in 2025

By Nazih Osseiran and Mohammed Benmansour

Grand Theft Auto, banned in Saudi Arabia until last year, is now being embraced not only by its gamers - a category that includes Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman - but also by its sovereign wealth fund, which the prince chairs.

This week, gamers in Saudi Arabia joined legions of fans around the world to play Grand Theft Auto VI upon launch — the first new release of the top-selling series since a Saudi ban was scrapped in 2025.

"Playing GTA VI in Saudi Arabia legally makes me so happy, because we're talking about a game that was banned," local content creator Thamer al Dairem said from a windowless, air-conditioned room, lit mostly by the bank of monitors displaying the game.

"We're talking about the biggest game in the world."

Support and investment in gaming by Saudi Arabia have been rising fast, not least from de facto ruler Mohammed bin Salman, often known by his initials MBS, who told Fox News in 2023 that gaming helped him disconnect and let off steam.

The Public Investment Fund (PIF), the sovereign wealth fund he chairs, owns a major stake worth over $2 billion in Take-Two Interactive , the US firm that owns Grand Theft Auto-developer Rockstar Games, LSEG Workspace data show.

CHANGING CUSTOMS IN CONSERVATIVE SAUDI ARABIA

In August, a consortium including PIF acquired gaming giant Electronic Arts for $55 billion. This month, gaming software provider Unity Software held talks with investors including the Saudi sovereign wealth fund on a potential buyout valuing it at around $25 billion.

PIF, which has spent the past year consolidating its gaming holdings into a subsidiary, Savvy Games Group, declined to comment.

MBS has been leading a campaign to open Saudi Arabia up and ease strict social and cultural norms that revolve around a conservative interpretation of Islam — a far cry from GTA VI's Vice City.

GTA VI advertisements have been appearing in some of Saudi Arabia's most popular shopping malls. One image shows the heroine wearing shorts and a crop top, her arm resting on her partner's shoulder — unthinkable a few years ago, when women were required to dress modestly and cover their hair.

MBS's wider reform plan, dubbed Vision 2030, is all about reducing reliance on oil and gas revenues, both in the economy and in state revenues, and PIF strategy is part of that.

"(It) is part of a diversified long-term investment strategy to capture value from industries it does not traditionally operate within," said Piers Harding-Rolls, who researches games at Ampere Analysis.

In Riyadh, al Dairem is now streaming Grand Theft Auto content and says that, while some of the depictions of violence, drugs and sex are extreme, the game is age-restricted and reflects another country.

"The city is Vice City, and it's representing Miami and the chaotic things that happen. For us Saudis, like, we know that it has nothing to do with us."

The gaming experience, on the other hand, matters hugely to him.

"When I saw the ads of GTA VI in the malls, I was so happy. If you'd asked me if I was ever going to see this, like, 10 years ago in Saudi, I wouldn't have believed it."

data.title: Rupee soars to 7-month high against the dollar, strengthens below 93 level
data.description:
The rupee soared to a seven-month high against the US dollar, strengthening below the 93 level on Friday. It was buoyed by continuous FPI inflows into the equity markets and softer crude oil prices even as the Dollar Index (DXY) was at a 20-month high.

The rupee gained 62 paise to close at 92.67 per dollar (USD) against the previous close of 93.29.

Thanks to the sustained FPI inflows into the equity markets, estimated at about $4 billion during the current week, the rupee has risen 157 paise overall this week against the dollar.

According to a Reuters report, oil prices fell on Friday and were set for a weekly decline on strong exports from West Asia  despite Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia’s capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures was at about $90 a barrel.

V Rama Chandra Reddy, Head - Treasury, Karur Vysya Bank, said the rupee’s sharp recovery reflects a decisive improvement in market sentiment.

“The turnaround is supported by a strong revival in FPI inflows, reportedly exceeding $12 billion during the month, softer crude oil prices and the RBI’s relatively measured intervention stance.

“The positive shift in currency sentiment is also likely to influence corporate hedging behaviour, with exporters increasingly inclined to accelerate forward dollar sales and lock in favourable conversion levels, while importers may defer their hedging requirements in anticipation of further rupee appreciation,” he said.

Kunal Sodhani, Head - Treasury, Shinhan Bank, noted that despite the US Dollar Index touching a 20-month high, the rupee has found support from robust FPI inflows, a reversal in global investment flows and softer crude oil prices. FPI inflows have approached $13 billion this month, marking an exceptionally strong return of foreign capital into Indian markets.

“The dollar demand-supply dynamics have also turned favourable, with exporters stepping up dollar sales after postponing hedges, while importers remain cautious on fresh purchases. The RBI’s special oil-related dollar window has further eased demand in the open market,” he said.

However, to prevent excessive rupee appreciation, the RBI may intervene through dollar purchases or encourage oil marketing companies to source part of their dollar requirements from the open market.

Sodhani estimated that technically, 91.80/92.10 remains a strong support for dollar/rupee, while a sustained close above 93.50 could signal a reversal in the near-term trend.

G-Secs yields soften

Meanwhile, yields of Government Securities (G-Secs) thawed, tracking softer crude oil prices as well as US treasuries. Yield of the widely traded 10-year benchmark paper (6.94 per cent GS2036) declined 6 basis points to close at 7.19 per cent against the previous close of 7.25 per cent.

Reddy said the G sec market also drew positive cues from the stronger rupee and softer crude prices, leading to buying interest and a moderation in bond yields. However, the downside in yields may remain constrained by elevated inflation expectations, the possibility of a further RBI rate hike in December and continuing global uncertainties.

The 10-year benchmark yield is likely to remain anchored around the 7.20 per cent zone, with a sustained decline depending on a sharper correction in crude prices, easing global volatility and moderation in inflationary pressures, per his assessment.

data.title: Ford taps India technology talent to develop global AI solutions
data.description:
India is emerging as a focal point in Ford’s global technology strategy, with teams there developing and modernising platforms used across its commercial vehicle and post-sale customer service businesses worldwide.

India has the largest technology workforce among Ford Pro and FCSD locations globally, and is key to enabling the company’s broader enterprise strategy, said Anaf Durrani, Chief Technology Officer for Ford Pro Tech and FCSD Tech.

Ford Pro faces commercial customers, from a single-van tradesperson to large fleets. It brings together vehicles, charging, software, service and financing. Its software platform, Ford Pro Intelligence, combines vehicle, charging and fleet data.

Meanwhile, FCSD looks after the ownership experience for Ford and Lincoln customers after the sale, through four businesses: Mechanical, Collision, Accessories and Extended Service. It also runs the global parts distribution network and supports dealer technicians.

Ford has over 12,000 people in FBS India and plans to hire about 500 in 2027 across Full Stack, Cloud, SAP, AI, and Data.

AI-native solutions

Ford is also looking to incorporate AI across its customer service capabilities while developing agentic AI-native solutions for commercial fleet customers. The company is adopting a two-pronged approach to address the shortage of AI talent by hiring externally and upskilling its existing workforce.

“We’re taking a multi-pronged approach: hiring wherever we can, given that demand is high and supply isn’t at that level yet, while simultaneously building up our current talent,” he added.

The India technology teams work as part of a global organisation, developing products jointly with colleagues in the US, UK, Europe and other regions. Their remit covers all markets in which Ford operates, including North America, Europe, South Asia and Latin America.

Durrani explained that reusability across teams frees up engineering capacity and accelerates product development, particularly as companies prepare for a challenging business outlook in 2027.

“As we modernise our technology, we’re looking at whether we can bring two similar systems together. If we can do that, the two teams working on them can free up capacity,” he said. “That capacity can then be utilised for other things we’re trying to build. There is so much demand as part of our modernisation and enablement efforts that it pushes us towards optimising our technology footprint.”

Currently, Ford Pro teams are looking to incorporate AI across its customer service capabilities, while developing agentic AI-native solutions for commercial fleet customers, whose requirements differ from those of individual vehicle owners.

“The goal is to have an AI-enabled and AI-powered workforce, with humans in the loop, where our people can leverage their curiosity and perspectives to build solutions,” Durrani said.

The FCSD technology team in India has contributed to Uptime Assist, a tool that uses live repair order data to identify bottlenecks in vehicle repairs and help dealers and Ford work together to reduce repair times.

The India team has also rebuilt Ford’s platform for approving extended service plan and parts warranty claims. The cloud-based system uses AI to autofill repair order details and provide real-time guidance on coverage, parts, labour, and recommended repairs. Low-risk claims are approved automatically, with most claims now being handled within four hours.

For Ford Pro, the company is developing agentic solutions tailored to fleet operators, who may manage multiple vehicles and face revenue losses when vehicles are unavailable.

“Commercial customers have a different use case compared to retail customers. A business may have multiple vehicles, whereas a consumer may have just one or two, depending on their family. We’re bringing more agentic solutions to address these specific use cases,” he said.

Ford is also exploring physical AI, although the work remains at an early stage. Durrani said the company’s approach was to identify customer problems before deciding where the technology could be applied.

“Many companies are exploring similar things. It’s about solving the right problems. We take an approach where we have to keep the customer journey in mind and think about the actual problem we’re trying to solve,” he said.

data.title: Infra sector growth hits new-series high of 10.9% in Oct, driven by higher iron-ore, electricity production
data.description:
Output of key infrastructure industries rose 10.9 per cent in October, the fastest pace in the new series, driven by double-digit growth in coal, iron ore, electricity and cement production.

According to the official data released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry on Friday, core sector production expanded by 0.8 per cent in October last year and 8.2 per cent in September 2026.

Among segments, iron ore output rose by 26.4 per cent, electricity by 21.6 per cent, coal by 23.1 per cent, and cement by 15.4 per cent.

However, production of natural gas (-7.6 per cent), crude oil (-4.1 per cent), and fertiliser (-12.2 per cent) fell during the month under review, the ministry said in the statement.

The cumulative growth rate of core sectors during April-October 2026 was 6 per cent compared to 2.3 per cent in the corresponding period of the previous year, it added.

The new series started in June. The base year has been shifted to 2022-23 and expanded from eight to nine sectors by adding iron ore.

Production growth of refinery products and steel slowed to 3.4 per cent and 7.3 per cent, respectively, in October.

Commenting on the data, Aditi Nayar, Chief Economist, ICRA Ltd, said while core output surged by 10.9 per cent in October 2026, the fastest pace in the new series, this was supported by a low base related to the shift in the festive calendar, with output having expanded by a marginal 0.8 per cent in the year-ago month.

While both coal and electricity benefitted from a favourable base as well as elevated demand for the latter, the robust growth in cement and steel output in October 2026 indicates that construction activity has remained healthy, she said, adding that cement output has expanded by double digits for the fourth straight month in October.

"Given the higher number of holidays, we expect the core output growth to cool to mid-single digits in November 2026," Nayar added.

data.title: Comstock Announces Grand Opening of Ebbitt House at Reston Station

() (“Comstock”), a leading real estate company specializing in the development, acquisition, operation, and management of mixed-use, transit-oriented properties and data center developments, today announced the grand opening of Ebbitt House at Reston Station. Located at 1860 Reston Row Plaza in The Row at Reston Station, the 12,000-square-foot restaurant opens its doors to the public today at 11 a.m. and will welcome guests daily. Reservations are now open via EbbittHouse.com and OpenTable.

Named after the original 1856 boarding house that gave rise to the legendary Old Ebbitt Grill, Ebbitt House marks the first-ever expansion of the storied brand outside of downtown D.C. in its 170-year history. Designed as a contemporary evolution of the D.C. landmark, the venue brings the signature Clyde’s Restaurant Group (“CRG”) hospitality, classic American fare, lively bar culture, and renowned raw bar to Northern Virginia’s premier mixed-use, transit-oriented neighborhood.

Ebbitt House features more than 400 seats spread across its 275+ guest dining room, two private dining rooms, and all-season patio. Two indoor bars anchor the main dining areas that are complemented by a dedicated outdoor patio bar. A full oyster and raw bar sits at the heart of the restaurant, carrying forward one of Old Ebbitt Grill’s best-known traditions, alongside a menu of elevated American classics that have drawn generations of guests to the original. Located steps from the Wiehle-Reston East Station on Metro's Silver Line, Ebbitt House is positioned as a destination for business lunches, after-work gatherings, and celebratory events alike.

“Ebbitt House is one of the most anticipated restaurant openings in Northern Virginia's history, and we are proud that CRG chose Reston Station for the first-ever expansion of such an iconic brand,” said Tim Steffan, Chief Operating Officer of Comstock. “Its arrival, alongside the JW Marriott Reston Station and our growing roster of best-in-class dining and retail, further cements Reston Station as the premier place to live, work, stay, and gather in the Dulles Corridor.”

The opening of Ebbitt House in Reston Station also marks CRG’s return to the area. CRG previously operated Clyde’s of Reston at Reston Town Center for more than 30 years, and several familiar faces from that team have rejoined to lead Ebbitt House, including General Manager Ajay Bhatia and Executive Chef Diego Ramirez.

"Reston has always held a special place in our history, and we are thrilled to return to this thriving community with a bold new chapter of the Ebbitt story," said John McDonnell, President and CEO of Clyde’s Restaurant Group. "Ebbitt House honors and expands upon the traditions guests love about Old Ebbitt Grill, from our renowned raw bar to our classic American hospitality, while introducing an elevated menu and an energetic, modern space tailored specifically for Reston Station."

Reston Station is among the largest and most prominent mixed-use, transit-oriented developments in the Mid-Atlantic region, covering approximately 90 acres spanning across the Dulles Toll Road and surrounding the Wiehle-Reston East Station on Metro’s Silver Line. data.title: Calabash Brings Its Day-to-Night Dining Vision to Life with Square
data.description:
Square today announced that Calabash, the Afro-Caribbean brasserie and bakery from acclaimed chef Camari Mick, has selected Square to power its day-to-night restaurant concept in New York City. Offering a bakery and brunch service by day and a full-service restaurant by night, Calabash chose Square for its ability to support each part of the business on one platform.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261118215743/en/

Photo of Chef Camari Mick, courtesy of Square

Located at 183 Christopher Street in the West Village, Calabash is Chef Mick’s first solo venture following her work as executive pastry chef at The Musket Room and Raf’s. A four-time James Beard Award semifinalist, Mick created Calabash to celebrate the food traditions and communities of the Black Atlantic. Her menu brings this vision to life through dishes including cornbread pancakes with salted maple sabayon and suya steak frites, pairing plantain fries with a suya-spiced au poivre sauce inspired by Nigerian suya. The space also features artwork by Black, Indigenous, and People of Color (BIPOC) women artists curated by gallerist Cierra Britton, extending the restaurant’s cultural storytelling beyond the plate.

One platform, from bakery counter to dinner service

Opening Calabash meant finding technology that could support two distinct service styles and consumer expectations, as the day begins with coffee and pastry orders, before transitioning to brunch, then giving way to seasonal prix-fixe dinners and carefully crafted nonalcoholic cocktails. By selecting Square, Calabash was able to meet the demands of a hotly-anticipated restaurant in one of New York City’s buzziest neighborhoods. Square for Restaurants and Square KDS help drive seamless front- and back-of-house operations. Square Register serves the bakery counter, while Square Stand supports lunch and dinner service. data.title: Bayer’s SUNHARBO® (asundexian) Now Available in the United States
data.description:
Bayer announced today that SUNHARBO® (asundexian), 50 mg tablets, is now available to order in the United States. Hospitals, health systems and pharmacies have immediate access to order the product for inventory. SUNHARBO is the first approved Factor XIa inhibitor in the U.S. and represents the first in a new class of medicine.1

SUNHARBO is indicated in combination with antiplatelet therapy to reduce the risk of stroke in adults with recent non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke (NIH Stroke Scale ≤ 15) or high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA).1

BAYER EXECUTIVE COMMENTARY
“The swift availability of SUNHARBO reinforces our commitment to patients,” said Nelson Ambrogio, President of Bayer U.S. Pharmaceuticals. “We are proud of the progress Bayer has made in bringing forward a new option for secondary stroke prevention.”

EXPERT COMMENTARY
“I want to see new secondary stroke prevention therapies available to healthcare professionals and their patients as quickly as possible,” said Mike Sharma, M.D., Principal investigator of the Population Health Research Institute (PHRI) OCEANIC-STROKE study, Senior Scientist at PHRI, and Director of the Stroke Program at Hamilton Health Sciences. “Now that SUNHARBO can be ordered for pharmacy inventory in the U.S., let’s recognize that we are taking another great step forward toward that goal.”

To support patients, Bayer is offering several programs designed to facilitate therapy initiation and continuity of care, including co-pay offers and patient education. For more information, visit here: https://www.sunharbosavings.com/.

The list price for SUNHARBO will be $748.50 for a 30-day supply. The list price does not reflect what most health plans or patients will pay. Costs will vary by health plan, and patients’ out-of-pocket costs will depend on their coverage, such as deductibles and copays. The list price may be subject to change without prior notifications.

Bayer is committed to making SUNHARBO accessible. If a patient cannot afford their prescription, Bayer may be able to help. Eligible patients may receive their Bayer prescription medicine at no cost through the Bayer U.S. Patient Assistance Foundation. For more information, please visit www.patientassistance.bayer.us or call to speak with a member of Bayer’s team at 1-866-2BUSPAF (228-7723).

About SUNHARBO® (asundexian)
SUNHARBO is a once-daily, first-in-class, oral Factor XIa inhibitor approved by the U.S. FDA and indicated in combination with antiplatelet therapy to reduce the risk of stroke in adults with recent non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke (NIHSS≤15) or high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA). SUNHARBO is the first approved Factor XIa inhibitor in the U.S. and represents the first medicine in a new class designed to target Factor XIa. SUNHARBO is an inhibitor of Factor XIa. Factor XIa inhibition reduces amplification of thrombin generation. In preclinical models, Factor XIa inhibition targets more pathological clotting (thrombosis) with lesser impact on normal clotting response (hemostasis).1

SUNHARBO was approved based on results from the pivotal Phase 3 OCEANIC-STROKE study where SUNHARBO significantly reduced ischemic stroke in patients after a recent non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack compared to placebo (6.2% vs. 8.4%; HR 0.74; 95% CI, 0.65–0.84; P<0.0001), both in combination with antiplatelet therapy.1

For additional information about SUNHARBO, healthcare professionals may visit SUNHARBOhcp.com. Please see the full prescribing information.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

CONTRAINDICATIONS and WARNINGS & PRECAUTIONS
None.

ADVERSE REACTIONS
Bleeding

  • The rate of International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) major bleeding was similar between SUNHARBO and placebo groups (1.6 vs. 1.5 per 100 patient-years).

  • The rate of ISTH major bleeding events within 90 days of treatment initiation was 4.5 vs. 3.1 per 100 patient-years in the SUNHARBO and placebo groups, respectively.

  • In patients planned to receive DAPT, the rate of ISTH major bleeding events was 1.9 vs. 1.5 per 100 patient-years in the SUNHARBO and placebo groups, respectively.

  • Among patients older than 75 years, the rate of ISTH major bleeding was 2.6 vs. 1.7 per 100 patient-years in the SUNHARBO and placebo groups, respectively.

  • In the high-risk TIA subgroup, the rate of ISTH major bleeding was 2.9 vs. 1.0 per 100 patient-years in the SUNHARBO and placebo groups, respectively.

  • The rate of gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding was higher in the SUNHARBO compared to placebo group (2.7 vs. 2.1 per 100 patient-years). The majority of GI bleeding events in the SUNHARBO group (74%) were clinically relevant non-major or minor bleeding, and the most frequent bleeding site was of rectal origin.

Diarrhea

  • The most frequently reported (> 3%) adverse reaction in SUNHARBO-treated patients was diarrhea.

Hepatic Enzyme Increased

  • SUNHARBO is associated with elevated hepatic enzymes. Substantial cholestatic liver injury or serious liver injury with jaundice were each reported in less than 0.02% of SUNHARBO-treated patients.

DRUG INTERACTIONS

  • P-glycoprotein (P-gp) substrates - Concomitant use of SUNHARBO increased the exposure to digoxin. For digoxin and sensitive P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may increase the risk of adverse reactions, follow the recommendation in their approved product labeling.

  • Combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers - Avoid concomitant use with combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers, which decreases SUNHARBO exposure and may lead to loss of efficacy.

USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS

Pregnancy

  • There are risks to the mother associated with untreated non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or TIA and risk of bleeding in the mother and fetus or neonate associated with use of anticoagulants during pregnancy.

Lactation

  • Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with SUNHARBO and for 5 days after the last dose due to the potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants, including bleeding.

Hepatic Impairment

  • Patients with moderate to severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B and C) may have intrinsic coagulation abnormalities and use of SUNHARBO in these patients is not recommended.

For additional important risk and use information, please see the full Prescribing Information.

You are encouraged to report side effects or quality complaints of prescription drugs to the FDA. Visit www.fda.gov/medwatch or call 1-800-FDA-1088.

About Bayer’s Stroke Franchise
Bayer is a leader in cardiovascular (CV) and cerebrovascular diseases, with a longstanding legacy of scientific innovation in the prevention and treatment of thrombotic conditions. Building on this heritage, Bayer is advancing innovative approaches to help address unmet needs in stroke, with a focus on the area of secondary stroke prevention and research into new pathways, including Factor XIa. Bayer aims to help shape the future of stroke care with products strategically positioned to help address critical unmet needs and drive significant long-term value. Bayer is working alongside the stroke community to better understand unmet needs and support patients and care partners across the stroke journey.

data.title: Apartments.com Releases Multifamily Construction Activity Update for Q3 2026
data.description:
Apartments.com, an industry-leading online marketplace of CoStar Group, Inc. (), released its latest U.S. multifamily construction activity update for the third quarter of 2026.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261120681612/en/

National apartment construction starts totaled about 76,000 units in Q3 2026, down 63% from the peak of nearly 206,000 units in Q1 2022 and the lowest quarterly total since 2012. Over the past 12 months, starts totaled about 342,000 units, the lowest annual pace since 2014 and roughly three-quarters of the units delivered over the same period.

As a result, the pipeline continues to shrink. About 593,000 units were under construction nationwide in the third quarter. That is roughly half the early 2023 peak of nearly 1.2 million and the 14th consecutive quarterly decline, returning the pipeline to mid-2016 levels.

"Developers are still breaking ground on far fewer projects than they're finishing, and that gap is reshaping the supply outlook market by market," said Grant Montgomery, national director of U.S. multifamily analytics at CoStar Group. "In places where starts have pulled back the furthest, the wave of new apartments that defined the past few years is giving way to a much thinner pipeline ahead."

Completions are also easing. About 446,000 units were delivered over the past four quarters, down 22% from a year earlier and 36% below the 2024 peak.

At the market level, New York City has the largest pipeline at about 46,000 units, followed by Dallas-Fort Worth at roughly 32,000. Relative to existing inventory, Miami leads with about 9% of its apartment stock under construction, followed by Charlotte and Fort Lauderdale at more than 6%.

The pullback is especially sharp in Texas, home to three of the six most active markets for apartment starts during the building boom. Combined starts over the past 12 months across Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston, Austin and San Antonio are down about 42% from a year earlier.
